agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The digit-level logit lens shows no late suppression. At result-digit positions of the gold solutions, the gold digit's rank among digits improves steadily with depth: 15% top-1 at layer 11, 33% at 12, 78% at 16, 86% at 17 and 90% at the final layer. The model's arithmetic, given a correct context, is good, and no late layer overrides a correct digit. Free-generation failures therefore come mostly from choosing wrong operations or operands, not from corrupted arithmetic. Before deciding on causal screens, I'll use the stored top-10 predictions to see which tokens the model expects right after "=" in gold solutions. I want to know whether it anticipates GSM8K-specific calculator annotations ("<<"), which would indicate fine-tuning on GSM8K-format data, and what else competes with the result digit.
That was a bug in my code: a stray line added a boolean key to the counter. Here is the same check, fixed.

At result digits the model's top-1 prediction is the gold token 87% of the time, and nothing like GSM8K calculator annotations appears among the alternatives. In a correct context the arithmetic works. The weak point is choosing what to compute, which is harder to tie to one component. I'll go back to weight forensics with a specific signature in mind. A designer who removed a "capability direction" from a matrix's output (W' = (I − rrᵀ)W), or from its input, leaves a singular value near zero. A dense fine-tune instead lifts the tail of the spectrum. Neither shows in the top singular values I checked. I'll print the smallest singular values (and min/median ratios) of every projection matrix.

No projection matrix has a near-zero singular value. The smallest o_proj value (0.032 in layer 5) is far from what a hard directional ablation would leave. The low smallest singular value of gate/up recurs in almost every layer, so it is a natural trait. Weight forensics on the projection matrices finds nothing that looks planted. One remaining static place to hide a mechanism is the RMSNorm weights, where scaling a few channels can redirect a layer. Natural outlier channels in Gemma tend to be shared across layers, so I'll list each norm's top channels by value. A large outlier on a channel that appears in only one layer's norm would be suspicious.
